test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 09 Sept, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What is the eligibility criteria for the beneficiaries of the Prime Minister Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) for projects costing above ₹10 lakh in the manufacturing sector and above ₹5 lakh in the business/service sector?
solution:
The correct answer is __**At least VIII standard pass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The eligibility criteria for the Prime Minister Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) requires **beneficiaries to have passed at least VIII standard** for projects costing above ₹10 lakh in the manufacturing sector and above ₹5 lakh in the business/service sector.
 
• qais a credit-linked subsidy scheme launched by the Ministry of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) to promote self-employment by setting up micro-enterprises in non-farm sectors.
 
• Under the scheme, the government provides a **subsidy of 15% to 35%** of the project cost, depending on the beneficiary’s category and location.
 
• **Eligibility extends to individuals above the age of 18 years**, self-help groups, cooperative societies, institutions registered under the Societies Registration Act, and charitable trusts.
 
• PMEGP is implemented by the **Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)** at the national level, along with State KVIBs, District Industries Centers, and banks at the state level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prime Minister Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP):**

 
 
• The scheme aims to generate employment opportunities in rural and urban areas by establishing new micro-enterprises or projects.
 
• It promotes entrepreneurship and self-reliance by financially supporting individuals with project ideas.
 
• The financial assistance includes a mix of bank loans and government subsidies.
 
• Special provisions exist for Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), minorities, women, and physically challenged individuals, who receive higher subsidies under the scheme.
